posts.title: Li Auto kicks off European push with golf partnership, names overseas i6 Li 6
posts.summary:
Li Auto confirmed that the Li i6 will appear as the Li 6 at next month's Paris Motor Show, where it will unveil its global product lineup and European business plans.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Li Auto has officially initiated its European market entry by partnering with the 2026 Solheim Cup in the Netherlands, utilizing a fleet of 20 Li i6 SUVs for VIP transport.
The company confirmed that its Li i6 electric SUV will be rebranded as the 'Li 6' for international markets, with a formal debut scheduled for the Paris Motor Show in October.

Li Auto's international strategy involves a regional product split, prioritizing battery electric vehicles (BEVs) for Europe while focusing on extended-range electric vehicles (EREVs) for the Middle East and Central Asia.
Management plans to disclose comprehensive European business strategies and product roadmaps at the upcoming Paris Motor Show, following the company's recent expansion into the Gulf region.

posts.title: Geely launches Galaxy TT sedan with lower starting price, longer range
posts.summary:
The Geely Galaxy TT starts at a limited-time price of 129,900 yuan ($19,170), with CLTC ranges of 640-725 km.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Geely launched the Galaxy TT sedan with an aggressive starting price of 129,900 yuan, undercutting its pre-sale pricing by 11% while simultaneously increasing the entry-level range to 640 km.
The vehicle lineup features an 800-volt high-voltage architecture and CATL's Shenxing TT LFP batteries, enabling 6C fast charging that achieves a 10% to 80% charge in under 12 minutes.
The model targets the competitive mid-to-large sedan segment with five variants, including a dual-motor Ultra version capable of a 3.8-second 0-100 km/h acceleration.
Advanced hardware is a key differentiator, with most variants equipped with LiDAR and Geely's proprietary G-ASD smart driving systems to compete with premium EV offerings.

posts.title: Powering AI is an architecture problem
posts.summary: On July 22, 2026, a transmission line fault in Ashburn, Virginia—the heart of the world’s largest data center cluster—knocked more than 3 gigawatts of load off the grid in seconds. And it wasn’t the first time. Two years earlier, a single failed surge arrester dropped roughly 60 Virginia facilities and 1,500 megawatts at once. No…
bullets: Recent grid failures in Ashburn, Virginia, demonstrate that data center power issues are increasingly architectural rather than just supply-side constraints.

AI data centers exhibit extreme load volatility, capable of swinging 70% of their power demand in milliseconds, which creates instability for traditional grid infrastructure designed for predictable industrial loads.

Legacy power stacks, which rely on internal UPS systems designed for short-term backup rather than high-frequency load conditioning, are failing to manage the rapid transients inherent in modern AI compute.
The industry must shift power protection strategies outside the building and into the power path to accommodate gigawatt-scale campuses and prevent cascading grid failures.

posts.title: Redefining Processes At Sub-2nm
posts.summary:
Discrete steps are being merged with others as dimensions shrink into the angstrom range.
The post Redefining Processes At Sub-2nm appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Manufacturing at sub-2nm nodes requires merging discrete process steps because shrinking dimensions have eliminated the margins previously used to manage structural stability and process variation.

Extreme fragility at the angstrom scale means that standard wafer probing can damage oxide layers or hybrid bonds, forcing manufacturers to adopt sacrificial pads or perform testing after wafer bonding.

The shift toward chiplet-based architectures to overcome reticle-size limits increases thermal density and structural stress, creating complex, overlapping manufacturing challenges that are difficult to isolate.

To mitigate the high risk of manufacturing defects in multi-die stacks, hyperscale data centers are shifting toward redundant server cluster architectures rather than relying solely on individual component reliability.

posts.title: Silent Data Errors Redefine Test Coverage And Fleet Maintenance Strategies
posts.summary:
Through better manufacturing screening, DFT for systems and fleet monitors, this major scourge on data center hardware is gradually being tamed.
The post Silent Data Errors Redefine Test Coverage And Fleet Maintenance Strategies appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Silent Data Errors (SDEs) are becoming a critical threat to large-scale AI training, with failure rates that become statistically untenable when scaled across millions of devices in a data center fleet.
Industry standards for reliability are shifting from historical commercial benchmarks of 100-300 DPPM toward automotive-grade quality of sub-1 DPPM to address the volatility of leading-node silicon.
SDEs are often caused by subtle manufacturing defects that remain undetected during initial testing but manifest as data corruption during long-duration, high-utilization workloads.
The financial impact of SDEs is significant, potentially costing data center operators billions in service disruptions, lost data, and the necessity to divert workloads to maintain system integrity.
